coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 12 units (the domain directory itself + 11 sub-domain directories, each containing an *-index.md) and 70 .md files, 881,950 bytes — matches the expected 12 units / 70 files exactly. Method: the root unit (index, cx, 9 domain-level leaves) and the 18.03/18.04/18.05/18.06 units were read in full prose; 18.07-18.14 were read via sandbox-derived extraction of Role Lens, Role Matrix, Behavior, Cross-Cut Details, Decisions and live Open Questions, with Deep Think rationale columns and cross-cut 'Touches' pointer lists read in compressed form (they carry restatement, not independent normative content). Four corpus-wide mechanical scans covered all 70 files without exception: (1) structural compliance — every unit directory has exactly one *-index.md and one *-cx.md, no folder has fewer than 2 children, every leaf carries a Role Lens and every index a populated Role Matrix; (2) all 167 Open Questions rows parsed for owner + deferral target — 141 live rows all carry both, the 26 flagged rows are struck-through RESOLVED entries, so Dimension 7 passes on tracked-deferral grounds almost everywhere; (3) a vague-normative and unfilled-placeholder scan (reasonable/adequate/N days/TBD/{PLACEHOLDER}); (4) a self-declared-unresolved-marker scan, which is what surfaced most of the findings below — this corpus reliably announces its own gaps in cross-cut synthesis prose, and the defect is that several such declarations carry no owner and no deferral target while the sibling Open Questions tables are otherwise disciplined. Dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are scored N/A across all 12 units: personas are owned by meta/personas.md and every index in this domain carries the explicit rule 'NEVER redefine a persona here — reference only'; project constraint axes are owned by meta/constraints.md; competitive positioning is owned by meta/competitive-landscape.md. None of those three files is in this domain's scope. Applicable checkpoints are therefore dimensions 1, 3, 5, 7, 8 = 5 per unit, 60 total. Devil's-advocate pass refuted five candidate findings that did not survive: (a) 18.16's 'blocks `advanced` state if a hard requirement is unmet' reads as a contradiction of the always-overridable freeze until 18.03.01 D-07 is read, which defines 'block' as 'requires an override that goes on the record' — 18.16's own override edge case is consistent with that; (b) the domain cx CX-13 'zero-hard-outstanding is the freeze precondition' is qualified in the same sentence by 'overrides record what wasn't resolved'; (c) 18.01's Operator lens 'Cannot drive any lifecycle transition' vs its explicit grant of venue-side cancellation resolves within the same table cell — the sentence governs the forward production lifecycle; (d) 18.03-cx:98 'Unresolved — 18.03.01 Q-02' and (e) 18.09-cx:33 '18.09 Q-02 and is unresolved' are both stale markers pointing at questions that exist and are struck-through RESOLVED with the substantive answer attached (D-06/D-07 and index Q-02/18.09.01 D-05 respectively), so neither forces an invention.

findings.claim: A rider version cut while a date is mid-advance has two different specified behaviours in two files, and the question is explicitly declared 'Unresolved' with no owner and no deferral target while every sibling question in 18.04 carries both.
findings.evidence: 18.04-riders/18.04-riders-cx.md:38 — '5. **State transition conflict**: Cutting a version while a date is mid-advance — does that date get v1 or v2? Unresolved; the safe default is that the advance holds its version at open, with an explicit "update to v2?" prompt.' CONTRADICTED BY 18.03-show-advancing/18.03.01-advance-checklist.md:131 — '| Rider amended mid-advance (18.04.04) | The rider version at advance open is the item basis. An amendment re-runs the diff as a change notice; it does not silently rewrite settled items | "Rider updated to v3 — 2 new items, 1 settled item affected" |'. The cx specifies an opt-in prompt that generates nothing until accepted; 18.03.01 specifies an automatic re-diff that generates new advance items immediately. Tracking is malformed: no owner, no deferral target on the cx declaration, and no Open Question covers it — 18.04-riders-index.md Q-01 (PDF import), Q-02 (rider ontology), Q-03 (contractual standing); 18.04.04-rider-templates-versioning.md Q-01 (template authorship), Q-02 (cross-act sharing), Q-03 (contractual version). 18.04.01-technical-rider.md:129 points at it as a dangling reference — '| Version cut while a member is mid-edit | The edit continues against the head; on save the member is told which version it landed in (CX-01 Q) |'.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether cutting rider v2 during an open advance auto-generates new advance items and re-diffs immediately, or holds the advance at v1 until a Producer accepts an 'update to v2?' prompt. The two choices produce different advance-item counts, different hard-outstanding gate values, and therefore different freeze eligibility on the same facts.

findings.claim: The roster attribute that separates touring party from local labour is named as a requirement in the cross-cut file but is established by no decision in the sub-domain that owns the roster, and the owning feature's Behavior specifies the unqualified roll-up the cross-cut warns against.
findings.evidence: 18.08-crew-credentials/18.08-crew-credentials-cx.md:55 — 'A local hire is on the roster but must not be in the party-size roll-up that drives catering (18.04.02 D-01), rooming (18.12.02) and per diems (18.13.01). A naive `count(roster)` would cater for three extra stagehands and book them hotel rooms. The roster's head count needs a *type* dimension — touring party vs local labour — or 18.08.01 D-04's downstream derivations are wrong.' The domain cx escalates it further at show-production-touring-cx.md:116 — 'This is the single most actionable modelling finding in the domain'. But no such attribute exists: 18.08.01-crew-roster-call-times.md Behavior:27 states 'Party size rolls up and is consumed by hospitality, rooming and per diems, which means a roster edit has consequences elsewhere' with no exclusion, its edge case at :53 states '| Local crew hired for a date | Appears on the roster via 18.08.03 with a scoped date and access |', and its decisions D-01..D-05 contain no type dimension — D-04 reads only 'Party size is a published input, and edits to it must be visible downstream'. 18.08-crew-credentials-index.md D-02 likewise: 'The roster's head count is a shared input, not local data'. The exclusion is encoded in exactly one consumer and absent from another: 18.12-travel-logistics/18.12.01-travel-accommodation.md D-02 — 'Party size derives from the roster, excluding local labour' — whereas 18.04-riders/18.04.02-hospitality-rider.md Behavior:26 reads 'Quantities derive from the party size (band + crew from 18.08.01)' and D-01 'Quantities derive from party size, never typed', neither excluding local labour. No Open Question covers it: 18.08 Q-01/18.08.01 Q-01/18.08.03 Q-03 are the persona question, 18.08 Q-02 is venue staff, 18.08.03 Q-02 is employment status.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the roster carries a party-type attribute, and which of catering quantities (18.04.02), rooming (18.12.02) and per diems (18.13.01) exclude local hires. Built literally from 18.04.02 D-01 an implementer caters for hired stagehands; built from 18.12.01 D-02 they do not — the same roster yields different catering counts, bed counts and payout totals.

findings.claim: The treatment of a receipt that syncs after the float period it belongs to has already been reconciled is declared 'Unresolved' with no owner and no deferral target, no default is given, and the outcome changes how much money a person is owed.
findings.evidence: 18.13-tour-finance/18.13-tour-finance-cx.md:37 — 'A receipt captured offline and synced days later lands in a float that has since been reconciled. Does it reopen the reconciliation? Unresolved — and real, because offline capture guarantees late arrivals.' The scenario is guaranteed by the feature's own design: 18.13.03-expense-receipt-capture.md specifies offline capture, and both reconciliation points are period-closing — 18.13.03:36 '4. At the end of the week the float reconciles: opening − payouts − receipts = the envelope.' and 18.13.01-per-diems-float.md:37 '5. At tour end the float reconciles: opening + income − payouts − receipts = what's in the envelope.' Neither states what a late receipt does to a closed period. Tracking is malformed — no owner, no deferral target — and none of the sub-domain's eight live Open Questions covers it: 18.13-tour-finance-index.md Q-01 (18 or 23 ownership), Q-02 (band P&L visibility), Q-03 (float regulation); 18.13.01 Q-01 (hold or record the float); 18.13.02 Q-01 (18 or 23); 18.13.03 Q-01 (build or integrate OCR), Q-02 (flow to 23). The nearest specified behaviour is a different case — 18.13.01:43 '| Float doesn't reconcile | The normal outcome; needs a variance with a reason, not silent absorption |' — which governs unaccounted cash at reconciliation time, not a receipt arriving afterwards.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a late-synced receipt reopens a closed reconciliation, posts to the next period, or is written off as a variance. Each produces a different float balance and a different reimbursement owed to the person who spent the money.

findings.claim: The wedge-ownership modelling decision is declared 'Not yet settled' and defers to 'Open Questions', but no Open Question in the sub-domain covers it — the pointer is dangling and the question has no owner or deferral target.
findings.evidence: 18.05-stage-plot-input-list/18.05-stage-plot-input-list-cx.md:73 — '1. **Shared state conflict**: Wedges are the shared object. Are they plot items that mixes reference, or mix outputs that render onto the plot? Provisional answer: the mix is authoritative (a wedge exists because a mix needs it), the plot positions it. Not yet settled — see Open Questions.' Reinforced at :106 — 'CX-03's ownership question (are wedges plot items or mix outputs?) is the one genuinely unresolved modelling decision in this sub-domain. It is small but it determines whether adding a mix can make an act not fit the stage.' The referenced Open Questions do not contain it: 18.05-stage-plot-input-list-index.md Q-01 (spatial editor vs structured list), Q-02 (console session-file export), Q-03 (versioning cadence vs the rider); 18.05.01 Q-01 (spatial canvas); 18.05.02 Q-01 (console export), Q-02 (RF coordination); 18.05.03 Q-01 (mix content depth), Q-02 (IEM/RF). The consequence is stated in the same file at :74 — 'Mix added on a wedge → plot item appears → footprint changes → stage-dimension diff may newly fail.' Downgraded from blocking because a provisional answer is supplied inline ('the mix is authoritative'), so an implementer has a stated default to build against.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether adding a monitor mix creates a plot item (and therefore mutates stage footprint and the 18.03.02 stage-dimension diff), or whether a wedge must pre-exist on the plot before a mix can reference it.

findings.claim: Whether a provisional gear loss mutates the manifest for remaining tour dates immediately or only on confirmation is declared 'Genuinely unresolved' with no owner and no deferral target, and every Open Question in the sub-domain is either resolved or about a different subject.
findings.evidence: 18.09-backline-gear-manifest/18.09-backline-gear-manifest-cx.md:74 — '5. **State transition conflict**: If the loss is provisional (might turn up tomorrow), does the manifest change now or on confirmation? Changing too early creates phantom shortfalls; too late means arriving in Leeds without a bass rig and no time to hire one. Genuinely unresolved.' Restated in the same file's agent notes at :104 — 'CX-03's timing question (provisional loss vs manifest mutation) has no good answer yet and has real consequences — a phantom shortfall or an unhired bass rig.' The sub-domain's Open Questions cannot absorb it: 18.09-backline-gear-manifest-index.md Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 are all struck-through RESOLVED, 18.09.01 Q-01 is RESOLVED, 18.09.03 Q-01 and Q-02 are both RESOLVED, and the only live question is 18.09.02 Q-01 ('Is backline rental supply dense enough outside major cities'). The related feature text establishes that losses are provisional but not the mutation timing — 18.09.03-load-out-loss-damage.md:45 '| Item found later | Losses are provisional until confirmed; closing the log is normal | "Found in [city] — closed" |'. Downgraded from blocking because the same cx supplies a usable default one section earlier at :73 — 'Loss confirmed → manifest updated for remaining dates → diffs re-run → new shortfalls → sourcing' — which reads as mutate-on-confirmation.
findings.forcedInvention: The trigger point at which a loss logged at load-out propagates into the remaining dates' manifests and re-runs their capability diffs: at provisional logging, or only at confirmation.

findings.claim: Two consequential timing windows in 18.18 are written as the literal placeholder 'N days' with no owner and no deferral marker, in a file that demonstrates the correct marker on a third window in the same section.
findings.evidence: 18.18-post-show-report.md:50 — '| Report never filed | Event still settles; venue truth loses the signal; a reminder decays after N days | "3 shows without reports — your venue history is thin" |'. And :58 — '| Operator never answers a right-of-reply | The reply prompt ages out after N days; unanswered discrepancies proceed on the corroboration path without the Operator's input, never blocked by their silence | Operator: "Reply window closes in 3 days" |'. The same file shows it knows how to track an undecided window — D-05 at :101 reads 'Filed reports are editable within a bounded window, then locked; all edits versioned … Exact window `[PENDING — /write-be-spec]`' — and neither live Open Question covers these two: Q-01 is the corroboration threshold (canonically owned by 16.05.04 Q-02) and Q-02 is cross-artist visibility. The second window is not cosmetic: it bounds how long an Operator's silence delays a correction to their own venue listing, and the row's own User Sees string asserts a concrete '3 days' that the rule text does not commit to.
findings.forcedInvention: The reminder-decay period for an unfiled report, and the right-of-reply ageing period after which a venue-data correction proceeds without the Operator.

findings.claim: The domain Role Matrix records the Operator as having no access anywhere in 18.06, which contradicts the write capability 18.06.04 grants them — an occurrence attestation that the domain's own provenance model is built on.
findings.evidence: show-production-touring-index.md:85 — '| 18.06 Setlist & Show Files | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ❌ None | 👁️ Read-only (published setlist only) |' with the legend at :101 defining '❌ No access'. Contradicted by 18.06-setlist-show-files/18.06.04-performed-setlist-capture.md Role Lens — '| Operator | Read-only + occurrence attest | Sees *that* a show happened in their room and can **counter-attest the occurrence** — a disinterested third party who was there, the strongest available witness that the event took place on this date at this venue (DT-06).' Also contradicted by 18.06-setlist-show-files/18.06.03-show-file-custody.md — '| Operator | Read-only (durations only) | Sees only that tracks exist and their durations, because that affects set timing and their curfew.' The sub-domain's own matrix agrees with the children (18.06-setlist-show-files-index.md records 18.06.03 and 18.06.04 as '👁️ Read-only' for Operator), so the domain-level row is the outlier. This is not absorbed by the matrix's 'Access icons are shorthand' disclaimer: '❌ None' and a counter-attestation write are opposites, not granularities. The capability is load-bearing — show-production-touring-cx.md CX-16 makes the Operator's attestation part of the provenance chain: 'Operator: attests occurrence only — the disinterested third party who confirms the show happened in their room'. The corpus escalates this exact class of index-vs-index disagreement to a tracked question elsewhere (18.03.01 Q-05, owner Agent, /create-prd-security), but no equivalent question exists for 18.06.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the Operator receives any 18.06 surface at all — specifically whether occurrence counter-attestation on the performed setlist is built, which CX-16 makes a precondition for the show record's attested (vs self-asserted) provenance grade.
